transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been having these thoughts that I forgot something important. Like with my aunt’s medicine, or things in my classroom not being set up safely. I know I probably did it right, but the doubt keeps coming back.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions to try and get rid of these doubts?

Yeah… I do. Before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll check the same things more than once. Like the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans… sometimes I just replay what I did in my head until I feel okay enough to go. It’s not a lot, but it can make me late.
Do you feel anxious when these doubts come back to you?

Yeah… I do. It’s mostly this uneasy feeling, like I can’t quite let it go. Even if I know I probably did the medicine right, or set things up safely at school, the thought pops back in and I get anxious until I check or think it through again.
Do you feel like checking or replaying these actions in your head is necessary to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I think so, in the moment. Like, before I leave, I feel like I have to check the pill organizer or the stove, or go back over what I did in my head, just to make sure nothing bad happens. Once I feel calm enough, I can move on… but sometimes it makes me late.
Do you have any other thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, beyond these doubts about forgetting something important?

Not really beyond that… it’s mostly the same kind of thought. Like I forgot something important, or I didn’t do it safely enough — my aunt’s medicine, or stuff in my classroom. Even when I know I probably did it right, it just kind of comes back.
Do you feel like these repeated checks or thoughts are helping to reduce your anxiety?

Yeah… I guess they do, at least for a little while. Like if I check the pill organizer or the stove again, or go back over what I did in my classroom, I feel calmer after. It’s just… sometimes I have to do it a few times before I can leave, and then I end up running late.
Are these thoughts and checking behaviors affecting your relationships or work as a teacher?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still doing my job and helping with family things, but mornings can take longer than they should. Sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed, like I’m behind before the day even starts.

And… lesson prep doesn’t feel as smooth lately. Even my evening journaling doesn’t feel as relaxing as it used to.
Do you feel compelled to perform any specific rituals or behaviors beyond checking things?

Mostly just the checking… before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll go back over the same things a few times. Like the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans… or I’ll sort of replay what I did in my head.

I don’t really want to, but I feel like I can’t move on until I feel calm enough. It can make me late sometimes.
Do you have any disturbing or intrusive thoughts that are not related to forgetting something or checking things?

Not really… not outside of that, I don’t think. It’s mostly the same nagging doubt that I forgot something important, like my aunt’s medicine or something in the classroom, even when I know I probably handled it. It just keeps coming back.
Are there any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind that don't have to do with forgetting something or checking things?

No… not really. It’s pretty much those same thoughts — that I forgot something important, like my aunt’s medicine or something in my classroom. Even when I know I probably did it, the doubt just kind of comes back.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that you try to ignore or suppress, beyond the doubts about forgetting something?
Not beyond that, no. It’s mainly those doubts… like I forgot something important with my aunt’s medicine or didn’t set something up safely in my classroom. I try to push it aside, but it comes back.
Do you feel like these thoughts and checking behaviors are interfering with your overall well-being or quality of life?

A little, yeah. I’m still managing work and family things, but mornings take longer than they should. Sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed, like I’m behind before the day even starts.

And… lesson prep or journaling at night just doesn’t feel as calm or helpful as it used to.
Are there any other areas of your life where you feel like these thoughts or checking behaviors are causing problems?

Mostly just the same areas… work and home. I’m still doing what I need to do, but mornings get stretched out, and then I can show up to school feeling rushed, like I’m already behind.

At night, lesson planning or journaling doesn’t really feel as easy or calming as it used to. It’s not… huge, but it does get in the way some.
Do you feel like these thoughts and checking behaviors are causing you a lot of distress?

I wouldn’t say a lot… but it does bother me. I’m still getting through work and family stuff, but my mornings take longer, and sometimes I get to school feeling rushed, like I’m already behind.

And at night, lesson prep or journaling just doesn’t feel as smooth or calming as it used to.
Are there any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind that are not about forgetting something or checking things, and that you find disturbing or unpleasant?
Um… not really. I can’t think of anything like that. It’s mostly the forgetting or checking-type worries, as far as I’ve noticed.
How long have you been experiencing these doubts and checking behaviors?
I’m not totally sure. It’s been… a little while, I guess. I didn’t really mark when it started, it just kind of became something I noticed more over time.
Are there any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind that you try to ignore or suppress?

Yeah… I guess I do try to push them away sometimes. It’s mostly that nagging feeling that I forgot something important—like something with my aunt’s medicine, or whether I set up the classroom materials safely. Even when I’m pretty sure I did it, the doubt kind of comes back.
Are there any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind that are not about forgetting something or checking things, and that you find difficult to control?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, nothing really comes to mind besides that same kind of doubt stuff.
Are there any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind that are not about checking things or forgetting something important?

Not really… it’s mostly the same thoughts I mentioned. Like I keep worrying I forgot something important, with my aunt’s medicine or the classroom stuff, even when I know I probably handled it. It just kind of pops back in.
